Project Management Tools Comparison

Asana · Trello · monday.com · Jira · ClickUp · Smartsheet — ten criteria in five groups

1. Overview

This document compares six widely used project-management platforms across ten criteria, grouped into Cost, People, Work Management, Connectivity and Insight. The table scrolls horizontally on narrow screens. Ratings use colored tags: Strong Adequate Limited.

Prices are approximate list prices per user per month on annual billing, based on publicly known pricing tiers. Vendors change plans often, so confirm current pricing before purchasing.

3. Recommendation

No single tool wins for every team. The right choice depends on team type, budget and how much reporting and governance you need.

🏆 Best overall: monday.com or Asana

For most cross-functional teams of 5–200 people, monday.com offers the best balance of ease of use, customization, integrations and reporting. Asana is a close alternative if you value structured task ownership over customizable boards.

💻 Software teams: Jira

Choose Jira for sprints, backlogs and agile reporting. Expect to invest in setup and training, and pair it with Confluence for documentation.

💸 Best value: ClickUp

ClickUp gives the most features per dollar, with unlimited members on the free plan. Plan time for configuration, and keep your setup simple to avoid clutter.

🗂️ Simplest start: Trello

Trello suits individuals and small teams with straightforward kanban workflows. Expect to outgrow it once you need reporting or complex dependencies.

🏢 Enterprise PMOs: Smartsheet

Smartsheet fits organizations with portfolio governance, resource planning and spreadsheet-centric habits. It costs more at scale and is less suited to small teams.

✅ Suggested next steps

  • Shortlist two tools based on team type.
  • Run a 2–4 week pilot with one real project.
  • Check integration needs (Slack, Google, Microsoft) and plan limits on automation.
  • Confirm current pricing and security requirements with the vendor.
